chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the compurgation (sworn endorsements), so he said: 'For all rights, the burden of proof is upon the claimant, and the oath is upon the defendant, except specifically regarding blood (murder)'

For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in Khaybar when the Helpers missed a man from among them, so they found him killed. So the Helpers said, 'So-and-so the Jew killed our companion.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to the seekers: 'Establish two just men from others, I shall retaliate by its entirety. So if you do not find two witnesses, then establish compurgation of fifty men, I shall retaliate by its entirety.'
So they said, 'O Messenger of Allah! There are no two witnesses with us from others, and we hate that we swear upon what we have not seen.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) paid the blood money from himself, and said: 'Rather, the blood of the Muslims is saved by the compurgation, so that when the immoral, mischievous one sees an opportunity from his enemy, he restrains himself in fear of the compurgation that he himself would be killed by it, so he refrains from killing him. Or else the defendant would swear an oath of compurgation of fifty men,

key_terms.الدَّمِ: Blood; specifically referring to homicide/blood money (diyah).
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: Blood money; compensation paid for homicide or injury.
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارُ: The Helpers; a specific group of early Muslims, here used as an example.
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: The burden of proof or evidence.
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: Compurgation; a legal procedure where fifty men swear an oath to establish liability.
key_terms.خَيْبَرَ: Khaybar; a historical location in Arabia where the Prophet resided.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on compurgation (qasamah) in cases of homicide without witnesses?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that 'al-qasamah' is a specific exception for homicide, contrasting with the general rule where the burden of proof (bayyinah) rests on the claimant and the oath (yamin) on the defendant. The Prophet’s instruction in Khaybar to accept fifty oaths when witnesses are lacking highlights the communal nature of blood liability in early Islamic jurisprudence. This mechanism serves to ensure justice and deterrence by imposing collective responsibility on the victim's group if they cannot identify the killer, a principle deeply rooted in Shia legal theory regarding qisas and diyyah.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya,

(The narrator) says: ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the compurgation (sworn endorsements), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With regards to the right, all of them, the burden of proof is upon the claimant, and the swearing of the oath is upon the defendant, except regarding the blood, in particular,
for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was in Khyber when the Helpers missed a man from them, so he was found killed. So the Helpers said, ‘So and so the Jew killed our companion’.

So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to the seekers: ‘Establish two just men from others, I<sup>saww</sup> shall retaliate by its entirety. So if you do not find two witnesses, so establish compurgation (sworn endorsements) of fifty men, I<sup>saww</sup> shall retaliate by its entirety’.
So they said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! There are no two witnesses with us from others, and we hate that we swear upon what we have not seen’.

فَوَدَاهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مِنْ عِنْدِهِ وَ قَالَ إِنَّمَا حُقِنَ دِمَاءُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ بِالْقَسَامَةِ لِكَيْ إِذْ رَأَى الْفَاجِرُ الْفَاسِقُ فُرْصَةً مِنْ عَدُوِّهِ حَجَزَهُ مَخَافَةُ الْقَسَامَةِ أَنْ يُقْتَلَ بِهِ فَكَفَّ عَنْ قَتْلِهِ وَ إِلَّا حَلَفَ الْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ قَسَامَةً خَمْسِينَ رَجُلًا مَا قَتَلْنَا وَ لَا عَلِمْنَا قَاتِلًا وَ إِلَّا أُغْرِمُوا الدِّيَةَ إِذَا وَجَدُوا قَتِيلًا بَيْنَ أَظْهُرِهِمْ إِذَا لَمْ يُقْسِمِ الْمُدَّعُونَ .
So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> paid it from himself<sup>saww</sup>, and said: ‘But rather, the blood of the Muslims is saved by the compurgation, perhaps when the immoral mischievous one might see a chance from his enemy, would keep aside in fear of the compurgation (sworn endorsements), that he himself would be killed by it. So he would restrain from killing him, or else the claimant would swear an oath against him, a compurgation (sworn endorsement) of fifty men, ‘We have neither killed nor do we know the killer’, or else be fined the wergild. When the killer is found in their presence, when the claimants do not swear’.
